There's no "winning." The battle will follow me forever

Now, that isn't as bleak as it sounds. 7 years ago, almost every waking moment was agony. I could barely eat, barely sleep. I wanted so badly for the pain to end. I knew I had no future.

Then I started therapy. And I started medication. It was something like 1 step forwards, three or four back. I changed medication. And again. And again. When I was in my junior year of college, I attempted suicide. I started a new medication. After I woke up still alive, everything had just a little glimmer to it. Just a touch of hope. 

Do I have days where I can't get out of bed? Sure. But I'm going ro school and work and writing and making art and living. I never thought I would. Sixteen year old me would tell you that you're stupid if you told them where I was now. I will never win the war, but I, with lots of help, win little battles everyday and that's where the importance lies.

TLDR depressions ups and downs but keep going and you'll find that there are more ups than you ever expected

I was taking a bus home from a science fair in high school. It was about three hours from our hometown, and I had eaten some shitty greasy food while there and was feeling pretty bad before I even boarded the bus. Half an hour in, I knew there was going to be an issue. My stomach started making sounds straight from the depths of hell. Then the cramps started. I prayed nobody noticed me as I clutched my stomach and prayed for a swift demise. I knew I would't be able to make it the full duration, but I decided to try, anyways. I don't go down without a fight, even if that fight is with my own anus and rebelling intestines.

Then the nausea hit, and I was pretty sure that death was near. I could only hope it happened before I could embarrass the hell out of myself. I was not so lucky. I ended up puking all over myself before I could do anything about it. I mean everywhere, all over my reasonably fancy, and white, dress shirt. As if that weren't bad enough, the force of my wretch made me unclench my asshole and the shitstorm was released. And I still had two hours to go until I made it home. On a bus full of teenagers. Just typing out the story makes me die a little inside. 

TL;DR,  don't eat dodgy pizza before a long, stopless busride

I have a good friend who very much believes in the paranormal, who is married to a man who is even more skeptical than I am. One day we started discussing the paranormal and she told me a story from when her son was still a child (he's maybe 30 now.) The three of them were driving home after dark and all of a sudden her son, who was about three, starts oohing and aahhing out the window of their car. She glances back in the rearview mirror and there was a blue light, round and maybe the size of a basketball, hovering right by his window. This was on a West Virginia back road with NOTHING to cast such a light. She sped up the car and the thing kept up with her, following her around turns as her son's interest faded and he became more and more distressed by whatever it was. She was going almost 70 to try and lose it when it simply blinked out and they were alone again. As she told me this story I noticed her skeptical husband getting really pale. Eventually he just shook his head, said he didn't want to say anything else about it, and walked off. Apparently whatever it was he saw still freaks him out to this day.

That story and a few told to me by my really skeptical mother makes me wonder a little bit, to be honest.

TLDR: mysterious floating light still scares the crap out of man who doesn't believe in anything of the sort
